old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the oft and leg stump.
new_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.

old_digest: When the Striker shall hit the ball, one of his feet must be on the ground behind the popping crease, otherwise the Umpire shall call “No Hit,” and no run shall be scored.
new_digest: When the Striker shall hit the ball, one of his feet must be on the ground behind the poppin" crease, otherwise the Umpire shall call “No Hit,” and no run-shall be scored.

old_digest: An over should always be finished, unless a wicket fall within two minutes of time (see. It is Umpire’s and not the Scorer's duty to call over. 8 Law 45), or unless there is a local rule extending the time.
new_digest: An over should always be finished, unless a wicket fall within two minutes of time (see Law 45), or unless there is a local rule extending the time. It is Umpire’s and not the Scorer’s duty to call over.

old_digest: All runs made from a “No Bail,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be’scored “No Balls,” and if no runs be made one run shall be added to that score.
new_digest: All runs made from a “No Ball,” otherwise than from the bat, shall be scored “No Balls,” and if no runs be made one run shall be added to that score.

old_digest: In 1911 an agreement was arrived at between the Counties that “Trial balls, if both batsmen are at the wickets, be not allowed in First Class Matches.’ This arrangement was approved and adopted by the M.C.C.
new_digest: In 1911 an agreement was arrived at between the Counties that “Trial balls, if both batsmen are at the wickets, be not allowed in First Class Matches.” This arrangement was approved and adopted by the M.C.C.

old_digest: 1st So often as the Batsmen, after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end. 2nd For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 44.
new_digest: A run is scored: 1st—So often as the Batsmen, after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end. 2nd—For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 44.

old_digest: Notes on Law 23 If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” 10 It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.
new_digest: If the ball rebounds off the pads or person of the wicket-keeper, without having first touched the bat or hand of the Striker, and the Striker is out of his ground the decision should be “Stumped,” and not “Run Out.” 10 It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.

old_digest: A Batsman may be out lbw, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.
new_digest: A Batsman may be out 1 b w, although the bowler is bowling round the wicket, if the case comes within this Law.

old_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an lbw with a breaking ball.
new_digest: It is sometimes only possible for a bowler bowling round the wicket to obtain an 1 b w with a breaking ball.

old_digest: (See Law 16, Note 3.)
new_digest: (Sec Law 16, Note 3.)

old_digest: The Striker being caught no run shall be scored, batsman being run out, that run which was being attempted shall not be scored.
new_digest: The Striker being caught no run shall be scored. A Batsman being run out, that run which was being attempted shall not be scored.

old_digest: When a run has been made off a no-ball the no-ball should be scored although the ball has been caught. 12
new_digest: When a run has been made off a no-ball the no-ball should be scored ( although the ball has been caught.

old_digest: If the Bail, whether struck with the bat or not, lodges in a Batsman’s Clothing, the ball shall become “Dead.”
new_digest: If the Ball, whether struck with the bat or not, lodges in a Batsman’s Clothing, the ball shall become “Dead.”

old_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in any way authorized by the Laws. He may have passed the bowling crease in his run, may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.
new_digest: A bowler may run a Batsman out, without having delivered the ball, in anyway authorized by the Laws. He may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before th owing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.

old_digest: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player, who may during the match, be incapacitated from illness or injury, but for no other reason, except with the consent of the opposite side. 13
new_digest: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player, who may during the match, be incapacitated from illness or injury, but for no other reason, except with the consent of the opposite side.

old_digest: If he shall take the ball for the purpose of stumping, before it has passed the wicket, or, if he shall incommode the Striker by any noise, or motion, or if any part of his person be over or before the wicket, the Striker shall not be out, excepting under Laws 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30. The Wicket-keeper shall stand behind the wicket.
new_digest: The Wicket-keeper shall stand behind the wicket If he shall take the ball for the purpose of stumping, before it has passed the wicket, or, if he shall incommode the Striker by any noise, or motion, or if any part of his person be over or before the wicket, the Striker shall not be out, excepting under Laws 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30.

old_digest: (See also Instructions to Umpires.) 14
new_digest: (See also Instructions to Umpires.)

old_digest: The In-going Batsman should meet the out coming batsman before he enters the Pavilion.
new_digest: The In-going Batsman should meet the out-coming batsman before he enters the Pavilion.

old_digest: No act on the part of the fielding side can cause a batsman to be out after the Umpire has called “Over,” but an appeal may be made within the allotted time. 15
new_digest: No act on the part of the fielding side can cause a batsman to be out after the Umpire has called “Over,” but an appeal may be made within the allotted time.

old_digest: A declaration of a first innings does not preclude a second innings.
new_digest: A declaration of a first innings does not prechide a second innings.

old_digest: After the actual commencement of play the ground may be again protected when necessary and shall be protected every night during the continuation of a match, but the covering shall be removed each morning, if fine, at 7 o’clock a.m The covering must not protect a larger area than 18ft by 12ft at each end, and must not protect more than 3ft 6in in front of the popping crease. 7
new_digest: After the actual commencement of play the ground may be again protected when necessary and shall be protected every night during the continuation of a match, but the covering shall be removed each morning, if fine, at 7 o’clock a.m. The covering must not protect a larger area than 18ft by 12ft at each end, and must not protect more than 3ft 6in in front of the popping crease.
